title: Europe’s Positive GDP Print Conceals a Slower Impulse
trigger: Eurostat’s 30 October flash estimate showed euro-area GDP growth easing from 0.6% q/q in Q2 to 0.4% in Q3, and EU growth easing from 0.7% to 0.5%.
limitations: GDP is a preliminary flash estimate subject to revision; growth figures are quarter-on-quarter, not annual rates. Elasticity and annual revenue are hypothetical; the scenario applies a quarterly GDP-growth difference mechanically to an annual sales base solely for sensitivity illustration.
formula: Observed growth momentum = Q3 q/q growth − Q2 q/q growth (−0.2 pp for both EU and EA). Illustrative revenue delta (€m) = annual exposed revenue × elasticity × (observed momentum + additional scenario shock) / 100. No causal estimate or time-series regression is implied.
decision: Use leading order-book indicators and customer concentration to test whether European growth deceleration affects the next two quarters of sales. Do not treat aggregate GDP as a direct export-demand forecast.
worked_example: Illustrative worked example: the observed −0.2 percentage-point change in euro-area quarterly GDP growth, applied with an assumed 1.5× revenue elasticity to €1bn of annual exposed sales, yields a −€3m sensitivity. It is not a revenue forecast.
